varieties.name: Heat-tolerant / bolt-resistant type
varieties.note: Kept from the existing crop-catalog.ts entry (previously uncited generic advice). Now cross-verified and made concrete below by Brigadier (Starke Ayres) and the KZN DARD warm/hot-area cultivar groups, which name the actual heat-tolerant varieties this generic note was gesturing at.

evidence.quote: Look for a variety specifically marketed as bolt-resistant for summer — 'triple red' and similar red-leaf types are noticeably more heat-susceptible, so save those for cooler-season sowings instead.

varieties.name: Brigadier

evidence.quote: A Fusarium-resistant lettuce with excellent heat tolerance for the pre-pack market. Summer harvest. Resistance to Fusarium race 1 and 2 with excellent heat tolerance

highveld.text: Cold, heavy-frost interior — sow Jan-Apr and Jul-Dec; favour cold-tolerant crisphead types (Del Rio, Del Oro, Frosty, Wintercrisp, Winter Supreme).

evidence.quote: Cold areas (heavy frost) Jan - Apr, Jul - Dec

high-mountain.text: Extrapolated from the same 'cold areas, heavy frost' sowing group as highveld — not separately confirmed for this specific zone.

midlands-mistbelt.text: Treated as a 'warm areas (light frost)' zone, sow all year; no cultivar-name-to-zone mapping found beyond the general cold/warm cultivar split.

lowveld-bushveld.text: Hot, frost-free areas sow Feb-Aug/Sept; favour warm-adapted crisphead types (Aviram, Commander, Tropical Emperor, Empire 2000, Summer Gold, Victory) or a marketed heat-tolerant hybrid like Brigadier.

subtropical-coast.text: Extrapolated from the same 'hot areas, no frost' sowing group as lowveld-bushveld — not separately confirmed for this specific zone.
